content:
The “BIM Guide for Local Authorities” will be presented to industry on 27 January, at 5:30pm, in a Webinar promoted by the Southern Regional Council of the Civil Engineering College of the Ordem dos Engenheiros.


This online seminar's main aim is to present the Guide and deepen the discussion around the challenge of implementing digitalisation in a local and regional context.


The document to be presented is the result of a project coordinated by the Research, Development and Innovation Director of BUILT CoLAB, António Aguiar Costa (Chair of CT197-BIM), and aimed to raise awareness among local authorities of Building Information Modelling (BIM). It also benefited from the contribution of several BIM professionals and academics in Portugal. This working group sought to define the fundamental concepts to support BIM implementation initiatives at a local authority, taking into account the complexity of this innovative way of working and its impact on organisations, particularly in organisations as diverse as these.


As such, “BIM in Local Authorities” can be seen as a guiding framework for implementing the digitalisation of construction and infrastructure, and BIM in particular. To find out more about the outcome, you can read the full document by visiting our website here.


It should be noted that the event will feature Carlos Mineiro Aires, President of the OE, Luís Machado, Chair of the Executive Council of the Southern Region of the OE, Miguel Azenha, lecturer at the School of Engineering of the University of Minho, Ricardo Veludo, Councillor for Planning, Urbanism and Citizen Relations at Câmara Municipal de Lisboa, António Miguel Castro, Chair of the Board of Directors of Gaiurb Urbanismo e Habitação, EM, Rita Moura, Chair of the AEC Cluster, Jorge Meneses, Chair of the Associação Portuguesa de Projetistas e Consultores, and also Fernando Pinho, Coordinator of the Southern Regional Council of the Civil Engineering College.


Participation in the event is free, but registration is required by 25 January and must be made here.
